behavior_constraints: New `anomaly` subcommand registered in main.go dispatch alongside existing subcommands
Reads aggregate JSON objects from stdin, one per line, in chronological order
Extracts global_mean_risk (float) and total_threats (int→float) from each snapshot
Baseline window = previous min(W, i) snapshots (indices max(0,i-W) to i-1)
Skip index if baseline contains fewer than 2 snapshots
Computes population standard deviation (divide by N, not N-1) per metric
Z-score rules: stddev==0 & value==mean → 0.0; stddev==0 & value>mean → 999.0; stddev==0 & value<mean → -999.0; else (value-mean)/stddev
combined_z = sqrt(z_risk² + z_threats²); emit anomaly only if combined_z >= threshold
Output sorted by combined_z descending, ties broken by index ascending
Each anomaly JSON object includes index, metrics{global_mean_risk,total_threats}, combined_z, baseline_count, direction, severity
entities.summary: Add a new `anomaly` subcommand that reads aggregate snapshots from stdin and detects dual-metric (global_mean_risk, total_threats) rolling-window z-score anomalies, emitting sorted JSON records above a threshold.

instruction_head:
### Extension: `secsentinel anomaly`

```
secsentinel anomaly [--window W] [--threshold T]
```

Read aggregate JSON objects from stdin (one per line, in chronological order as output by `secsentinel aggregate`). Detect statistical anomalies using a dual-metric rolling z-score approach.

**Algorithm:**
